subject: southern ground hornbill
title: This Bird Lays Two Eggs, but Only Ever Feeds One Chick

scenes.text: This bird lays two eggs, and only ever feeds one chick.
The southern ground hornbill stands a metre tall, and kills venomous snakes with its beak.
In most nests, the female lays two eggs, three to five days apart.
When the second chick hatches, the adults simply ignore it. Within days, it dies of thirst.
Scientists think the second egg is just a backup.
And the first chick is precious. On average, a group raises one chick every nine years.

description:
The southern ground hornbill usually lays two eggs, but the group only ever raises one chick; the second is ignored and dies of dehydration within days.
These metre-tall birds hunt on foot in groups and kill snakes and tortoises with their beaks. On average a group fledges one chick every nine years.
Why do you think they bother laying the second egg?
first_comment: Wild ground hornbills can live up to 40 years, which is how a group gets away with one chick a decade. Would you call the parents cruel or smart?
